why_it_matters: Closes half of the 0124 route-A program IN THE MACHINE: the S3 left leg of G-hs3-left - the actual analytic work at the left point (1/2 - d0 + i t) - is no longer an open assertion but a body theorem at an EXPLICIT per-point schedule, with the endpoint-face shape (BwireR + MrLift) already composed (t4l_face_left_body/band). This is the left-flank twin of the 0116-0120 right-flank closure, at the cost S7 predicted: the schedule is per-point ((n4 t)^(1/(2 sigma)) - unbounded as d0 -> 1/2, consistent with t4l_schedDiverge) instead of the uniform wire. The pre-check + formal pair is clean: max termwise ratio 1.0000 (T1 equality by construction - the schedule is EXACT, not slack), T3 pin headroom ~2.47x, sigma = 0 excluded as the named barrier. The equally important negative: the pre-check's squeeze-window measurement shows the S1 leg cannot be closed by the tuned-tail Qside on the band (devProg / wire >= 1.11 at the band edge, growing to ~1.1e4 by d0 = 1/2). So G-hs3-left does NOT dissolve into one body theorem; it splits: S3-left machinable (done, 0125), S1 / band-emptiness residual (S9, pending the B6 cross-check on the P1-P4 pin family's role). Structural lesson (S8 repair log, in the card): in the pinned mathlib, linarith/nlinarith silently fail on Nat.cast-numeral times variable terms until norm_num normalizes the cast; norm_num cannot prove nonnegativity through Real.sqrt (use positivity); the mul_le_mul_of_nonneg left/right pair splits on FACTOR POSITION, not just sign - the factor side must match the goal term exactly, and div_le_div_iff0.mpr puts the denominator on the right (so close with the _right variant).
